items.title: County Council Report - Councillor Steve O'Neill - County Ward 4
notes: provided an update on the changes to recycling currently underway, including a minimum user fee for waste facilities and a transition to producer responsibility for the blue box program. He indicated beginning January 1, 2025, a $10 minimum user fee will apply to all waste materials brought to Wellington County waste facilities and further explained, this fee is intended to reduce landfill use and encourage residents to use curbside collection.

Councillor O’Neill highlighted the new automated speed enforcement camera expected to be deployed in key areas starting in early 2025. He indicated signage will be installed 90 days prior to the activation of the cameras to ensure residents, commuters and visitors have sufficient notice before the program begins.
Councillor O’Neill responded to questions regarding leaf drop off at the transfer stations and continuation of the yellow bag garbage system.

items.title: Genevieve Scott, Cuesta Planning Consultants Inc.
notes: re: item 11.5 Settlement Area Boundary Expansion Recommendation Report

Genevieve Scott, Cuesta Planning Consultants Inc., on behalf of Breymark Homes at 965 Gartshore Street, Fergus, provided an overview of the development concept and outlined the key policy considerations.
She indicated the site represents a logical addition to Fergus, represents good land use planning and should be considered favourably by the Township.

items.title: David Galbraith, Up Consulting Ltd.
notes: re: item 11.5 Settlement Area Boundary Expansion Recommendation Report

David Galbraith, Up Consulting Ltd., on behalf of Polocorp, at 968 David Street North and 6581 Highway 6, Fergus, spoke in support of the inclusion of the southern lands and outlined the merits of including the additional northern lands at 6581 Highway 6. He indicated the inclusion of the additional northern lands is appropriate and represents sound land use planning, which will support the efficient use of land, establishment of a mixed-use complete community, and provide opportunities for the establishment of larger community uses, including a central park connected to Gibbons Drive Park by a series of pedestrian pathways.

items.title: Marcus Gagliardi, Cachet Homes
notes: re: Item 11.5 Settlement Area Boundary Expansion Recommendation Report

Marcus Gagliardi, Cachet Homes appeared regarding Item 11.5 Settlement Area Boundary Expansion Recommendation Report for lands at 6583 Irvine Street and 7581 Nichol Road 15. He highlighted the location of the subject lands and the merits of including these lands within the boundary expansion. He suggested homeownership should not be out of reach for young people today.

items.title: Rob Stovel, Stovel Associates
notes: re: Item 11.5 Settlement Area Boundary Expansion Recommendation Report
Rob Stovel, Stovel Associates appeared before Council regarding Item 11.5 Settlement Area Boundary Expansion Recommendation Report.
He requested 5 hectares just south of the high school and east of the south Fergus secondary plan be included in the expansion boundary.

He plans to provide mixed-use and affordable housing. He highlighted the merits of including these lands, as they are close to the high school, local elementary schools, and the Centre Wellington Community Sportsplex.

items.title: Outdoor Water Use By-law Information Report
notes: Report from D. Masiero, Manager of Water Services and Environmental Sustainability

Dino Masiero, Manager of Water Services and Environmental Sustainability provided an overview of the report, indicating the new by- law includes a tiered system based on drought severity levels with more stringent restrictions during drought conditions. He explained in order to establish the tiers, it is required to recognize the existing provincial Ontario Low Water Response Program.
D. Masiero responded to questions regarding the frequency of a Level 3 drought conditions and the public engagement strategy planned to educate the community.
Councillor Wilton, having declared a conflict of interest pertaining to the next item, left the room and therefore did not participate in discussions nor did she vote on the matter.

items.title: Deputy Mayor Lustgarten-Evoy indicated a notice of reconsideration and
notes: subsequent motion has been brought forward by Councillor Wilton, however, before the proposed motion can be considered, Council must first agree with 2/3rds majority to waive the procedural requirement for giving notice, and agree to reconsider the previous decision of Council adopted at the October 15, 2024 meeting to endorse a new outdoor refrigerated multi-use surface with mechanical and storage buildings for Bissell Park.

Deputy Mayor Lustgarten-Evoy stated if agreement is obtained to waive the notice provision of Procedure By-law 2021-31 for reconsideration, and agreement is achieved to reconsider a previous decision, Council must either amend the previous decision or rescind it and consider new action.

The purpose of reconsidering a vote is to permit the correction of hasty, ill-advised or erroneous action, or to take into account added information or a changed situation that has developed since the taking of the vote.
Councillor Adams raised a Point of Order.

Deputy Mayor Lustgarten-Evoy requested Councillor Adams state the substance of and the basis for the Point of Order. Councillor Adams pursuant to Section 3.8 of the Procedure By-law, indicated both motions are a deviation or departure from the rules in the procedure by-law, she questioned the validity of both motions and suggested motion 1 proposes to amend the decision and motion 2 proposes to amend and rescind the motion which is contrary to Section 7.2 of the procedure by- law.
Deputy Mayor Lustgarten-Evoy called for a recess to confer with staff.
Deputy Mayor Lustgarten-Evoy resumed the meeting and ruled the Point of Order put forth by Councillor Adams to be out of order. She indicated support for dividing the motion.
Councillor Adams respectfully appealed the ruling of the Chair and requested Members of Council decide whether to uphold or overturn the decision of the Chair.
Council voted and upheld the ruling the Chair.
